key: Kuper, Saran & White — Rapid Evidence Assessment (REA) of What Works to Improve Educational Outcomes for People with Disabilities in LMICs || Original 2018 publication (Campbell Collaboration and International Centre for Evidence in Disability, DFID-commissioned, published July 2018). No formal update or superseding standalone REA found. The Hunt 2025 systematic review is the successor evidence synthesis this REA was designed to precede, but it is a different document type and does not replace the REA's citation identity

key: Saran, White & Kuper — Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness of interventions for people with disabilities in LMICs || Original publication: Campbell Systematic Reviews 16(1):e1070, 9 January 2020. A corrigendum was published 12 July 2020 (Campbell Systematic Reviews 16(3), DOI 10.1002/cl2.1104) correcting the income-country distribution figures: 'over half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from lower-middle income countries' was corrected to 'almost half (n=50)…' and the upper-middle income country count was corrected to n=48 (not n=50), with low-income countries confirmed at n=9. A separate but related EGM cited as Saran, White & Kuper 2020, Campbell Systematic Reviews 16(9):e1111 (DOI 10.1002/cl2.1111) also exists and may be a broader or updated version, its relationship to e1070 could not be fully established from available sources
